**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** 12. Laughing loudly

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dutiyaujjagghika* is the twelfth training rule of the Sekhiya section of the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga in the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It establishes monastic etiquette concerning loud laughter while in inhabited areas. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate wide representation of this rule across Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. Within the Pali canon, it corresponds to Bhikkhu Pātimokkha Sekhiya 12, Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha Sekhiya 12, and the corresponding rules in the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Parivāra [SuttaCentral]. Across non-Theravāda lineages, parallels survive in Sanskrit, Chinese, and Tibetan traditions, including the Sarvāstivāda Pātimokkha, the Mahīśāsaka Vinaya and Pātimokkha traditions for monks and nuns, the Dharmaguptaka Vinaya and Pātimokkha texts, the Mahāsāṅghika and Lokottaravāda Vinayas and Pātimokkhas, and the *Upāliparipṛcchā* [SuttaCentral]. Automatically computed text reuse identified by DharmaNexus shows 107 matches across 39 other Pali texts, largely reflecting standard regulatory framing shared with adjacent Sekhiya rules (such as Sekhiyas 4, 6, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, and 20), especially within segment ranges §0.1–1.15 [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches are recorded at significant thresholds in DharmaNexus [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
